name: m5-persistent-salted
description: `m5-persistent` again after fixing a benchmark artifact: with one seed, every compile against a persistent table repeated the earlier compiles' hashes, so each lookup walked and dereferenced all their equal-hash dead entries (and `Reference.get` during marking kept those referents alive). Persistent compiles now salt their symbols' hashes, making the same shapes with new hashes, as a resident compiler's successive runs make new symbols. Fresh compiles are unchanged.
Persistent tables (one per thread for the whole fork) against fresh ones, at 2 GB, `-Xmn256m`, 4 MB regions. Graal 25.4.4 on the M5 Pro, one fork per table and round.

variantDescriptions.chunked-weak-rejuv: `chunked-weak`, copying each element chunk written at least 256 times since the last GC, so chunks stay young
variantDescriptions.chained-weak-fresh: control: `chained-weak` with a fresh table per compile, at the same heap settings
variantDescriptions.chunked-weak-fresh: control: `chunked-weak` with a fresh table per compile, at the same heap settings
